patterns.pattern: Only authorized users can access or manage their own data and resources; vendors cannot access or alter data belonging to other vendors.
patterns.example_phrasing: Vendors can only manage their own products, orders, and payouts; access to other vendors' data is prohibited.

patterns.pattern: Administrators/superusers have elevated privileges to manage marketplace-wide settings, vendors, categories, commissions, user roles, registration, payments, and rules.
patterns.example_phrasing: Admin manages vendor registration, publishing, payment disbursement, commissions, and has override on reviews.

patterns.pattern: Buyers must have a registered and authenticated account to make purchases or bookings.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only buyers with accounts are allowed to purchase.

patterns.pattern: Listings, bookings, or inventory cannot be purchased or booked for more units/seats than are available in current stock; stock is atomically reduced on successful purchase, increased on restock or cancellation.
patterns.example_phrasing: Cannot purchase more units than available stock; stock decreases on purchase and increases on restock/cancel.

patterns.pattern: Vendors/providers can manually adjust their own inventory, stock or seat availability, but only for their own listings.
patterns.example_phrasing: Providers can manually adjust stock and seat availability for their own products.

patterns.pattern: Booking and order workflows have configurable states (pending, active, expired, canceled, completed); transitions are automated by rules and parameters (e.g., expiration, acceptance delays).
patterns.example_phrasing: Bookings expire or are automatically validated after configurable delays; cancellations handled per policy.

patterns.pattern: Commission, fee, and VAT rules are flexible: rates can be set globally or per vendor/user and calculated automatically as part of transactions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Commission and fee rates are automatically calculated per vendor or globally for every transaction.

patterns.pattern: Notifications (email, in-app) are sent based on lifecycle triggers (e.g., messages, bookings), subject to user/email verification; custom notifications require integration.
patterns.example_phrasing: Email notifications only sent to verified addresses, triggered by events like new messages; extra integrations optional.

patterns.pattern: Vendor onboarding and verification is required before listing or managing offers.
patterns.example_phrasing: Sellers must be verified by the marketplace before they can offer products.

patterns.pattern: Admin can assign user roles with scoped access to channels or domains within the app.
patterns.example_phrasing: Administrators can grant custom roles limited to specific channels.

patterns.pattern: Listings/prices can be synchronized across channels out-of-the-box or per setting, but remain consistent for the same product variant.
patterns.example_phrasing: Prices can be synced for identical products across vendor channels if enabled.

patterns.pattern: Vendor and admin roles each have dedicated interfaces (frontend dashboard for vendors, backend for admin).
patterns.example_phrasing: Vendors access their dashboard, while only admins can use the backend.

patterns.pattern: Marketplace supports a broad scope of offerings: physical goods, digital content, services, bookings, rentals, and datasets.
patterns.example_phrasing: Vendors can offer physical, digital, rentals, services, bookings, and data packages.

patterns.pattern: Marketplaces allow flexible shipping and fulfillment rules per vendor, zone, or product type.
patterns.example_phrasing: Shipping policies are managed per vendor or zone.

patterns.pattern: Coupons, bookings, and cancellation/refund policies can be configured at the seller or marketplace-wide level by the appropriate party (vendor or admin).
patterns.example_phrasing: Vendors can create their own coupons; admins set global ones; refunds/cancellations handled by settings.

patterns.pattern: Sensitive price and monetary data are stored using standardized formats (e.g., cents, default currency) to ensure accuracy across financial computations.
patterns.example_phrasing: All prices stored in cents and in the default currency for consistency.

patterns.pattern: Data packages/datasets and their metadata may be versioned, tagged, and validated for integrity on publishing; deletion may be reversible (restore support).
patterns.example_phrasing: Data packages can be versioned, tagged, and restored after deletion; validated on publish.

patterns.pattern: Publishing and discoverability scope is configurable: resources (like datasets, listings) can be made public or limited to select users/groups.
patterns.example_phrasing: Publishing a dataset can make it public or limited to specific people.

patterns.pattern: All core integrations (e.g., payments, notification, search) are modular and pluggable; default operation is possible without external services.
patterns.example_phrasing: Integrations like payment and email are optional and can be swapped out.

patterns.pattern: Public browsing, search, and filtering of products, datasets, vendors, and activity metrics are allowed; private/entity-restricted resources have controlled access.
patterns.example_phrasing: Buyers and consumers can browse, search, and filter publicly available resources.
